result.title: Combining Relevant Expert Knowledge Using Mixtures of Feedback Fuzzy Cognitive Maps
result.summary: A neuro-symbolic system should combine only relevant answers from expert agents or other knowledge sources. Using only relevant experts for a given input query becomes ever more important for accuracy and scalability as the knowledge network grows and connects ever more knowledge sources. We extend the standard definition of relevance from the legal theory of evidence: An answer is relevant if and only if it is both probative and material for the matter at hand given the knowledge available. We apply this relevancy scheme to mixing the feedback fuzzy cognitive maps (FCMs) of real or artificial experts. The expert FCM directed causal graphs mix or combine into a common knowledge network. We compare the equilibrium limit-cycle predictions or answers of the experts to the answers of the mixture FCM and then estimate the probative status of answers by their difference or variation. A new Bayes-like theorem de-mixes the knowledge mixture into corresponding posterior-like FCMs that also allow relevancy-based comparisons. The result is a final set of relevancy mixing weights that produces a relevancy-mixed FCM knowledge network for the given query. So different queries produce different relevancy-mixed FCMs. We demonstrate this relevancy approach using generated synthetic FCMs from an actual 13-node expert FCM that models the causes and feedbacks of ischemic-stroke risk.

AI.brief_summary: 该文把法律证据理论中的相关性（兼具证明力与实质性）形式化地用于神经符号系统，通过比较各专家反馈模糊认知图与混合 FCM 的极限环预测差异来估计答案的证明力，再用类贝叶斯去混合得到查询相关的混合权重，并在合成样本与一个 13 节点缺血性中风风险 FCM 上演示。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“按查询只取相关来源”、以预测差异衡量各来源贡献的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与多分支 latent 的贡献分配提供概念性参照，但领域相距较远，迁移可行性有待核查。
